answer: Each identity faces a quartz-clocked observation challenge: at a random minute it must fetch and sign one live public fact, such as a commodity price or a weather reading, within a sixty-second window. Verified answers mint jade-stamped observation receipts bound to the long-lived key. Newcomers start in a frozen tundra of tiny audited jobs until they hold enough receipts. A farm sharing one data pipeline submits identical or stale readings, which correlation flags at once; each exposed fake burns its bond, so faking many identities costs many live pipelines plus many bonds.
